# #77 — P1: Fix openbrain-memory live-write redaction and replayable spool semantics

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-06-11T01:15:56Z
Updated: 2026-06-11T01:42:39Z
Closed: 2026-06-11T01:42:39Z

---

## Context
The post-merge swarm review of PRs #72-#76 found that `AgentMemory._call_write()` redacts payloads before sending them to Open Brain and then also spools redacted payloads on failure.

## Findings
- `python/openbrain-memory/src/openbrain_memory/agent.py` builds a redacted payload and sends that to the live client call.
- Legitimate memory content matching secret/token/password patterns can be silently persisted as `[REDACTED]`.
- Failed writes are spooled after redaction, so replay cannot faithfully restore the original write.
- This conflates three separate policies: live storage, diagnostics/log safety, and offline replay durability.

## Impact
The package can corrupt legitimate memories and make the JSONL spool lossy while still presenting it as a recovery path.

## Acceptance criteria
- Live Open Brain writes use the original caller payload unless an explicit configured write policy says otherwise.
- Logs/errors/spool entries are redacted or otherwise protected without mutating live writes by accident.
- Spool replay contract is explicit: either exact replay with protected/encrypted payloads, or documented audit-only/non-replayable behavior.
- Tests prove memory content is not silently redacted on successful live writes.
- Tests prove failed-write spool behavior is either replay-faithful or clearly marked non-replayable.
